messages:
sasha: Quick thread — trying to reconcile p99 vs throughput numbers from replay vs synthetic. Spoiler: tails diverge quite a bit.

devon: Can you paste the exact configs + input distribution you used for both runs?

sasha: Sure. Replay was ~3 days of prod traces (sampled), synthetic was poisson arrivals with mean=7rps. Microbatch config: 
```
microbatch_size: 4
batch_timeout_ms: 8
enable_kv_prefetch: true
max_batch_tokens: 2048
```

perf-bot: PERF SUMMARY (1751345678): replay -> p95=210ms p99=610ms tps=140; synthetic (poisson) -> p95=190ms p99=320ms tps=180.

marco: That delta on p99 screams KV/cache churn + batch-shape skew. Replay has lots of repeated prefixes which should warm KV, but microbatching + eviction can cause big spikes.

anika: Also worth calling out kernel selection. We saw fused-attn kernels reduce median but sometimes increase tail when sequence lengths vary within a batch. Did you force kernel pinning?

sasha: We tried both pinned and auto. Observations: fused kernels help median ~15% but p99 sometimes +20% on replay due to uneven per-sample token counts causing stragglers inside a microbatch.

liz: TL;DR: replay shows the realistic tail SLO risk; synthetic is useful to stress isolated subsystems. Both are needed. Also compute rolling-window percentiles, not just a single p99 over the whole run.

devon: For benchmark methodology proposal:
1) Replay (SLO validation) — run real trace to check end-to-end tail.
2) Synthetic targeted tests — isolate batching, kernels, kv by controlling arrival shape and seq length.
3) Microbench kernels offline (flamegraphs, topo) to guide kernel selection. :white_check_mark:

marco: @sasha can you upload the flamegraph for the worst p99 bucket? Even a rough svg helps.

sasha: Uploaded: https://perf.internal/reports/1751345678/flame.svg — main hotspots: kernel_fused_attn, kv_eviction_worker, batch_coalescer.

perf-bot: CI-REGRESSION: current PR #5982 increases replay p99 by 12%. Tagging @eng-releases and @eng-sre.

anika: Proposed quick canary: kv_prefetch=false + microbatch_size=2 + batch_timeout_ms=6. That should reduce eviction churn and lower variance.

sasha: Starting canary now on dedicated pool. Link: https://deploys.internal/canary/1751345678 — will post numbers in ~5m.

liz: Good. After canary, capture the methodology + config matrix in a short doc and put in eng-runtime/benchmarks so it's reproducible. Also note that p95 tuning is not sufficient for user-facing SLOs — focus on p99 for SLO sign-off.

devon: One more: when reporting p99 include sample counts and CI (bootstrapped error bars). p99 is noisy for small N.

marco: Agreed. Also include per-microbatch-size breakdown (1,2,4,8) so we can map latency vs throughput curve.

perf-bot: CANARY RESULT: kv_prefetch=false, microbatch=2 -> replay p95=220ms p99=360ms tps=130. (baseline replay p99=610ms).

sasha: Nice — big tail improvement. Will iterate on kernel scheduling + batch shape to recover TPS. Thanks all. :rocket:
